summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a specification and driver layer that lets AI agents like Claude discover, control, and orchestrate lab and manufacturing instruments (liquid handlers, robotic arms, microscopes, PCR machines) via MCP, CLI, or code, and shared early results from partners including Genentech and a University of Washington lab.

mechanisms.reason: The standard demonstrates agents autonomously sequencing, monitoring, error-recovering and adaptively controlling physical lab instruments in real time, a new class of tool-use task beyond software-only agents.
mechanisms.quote: The agent can sequence steps across instruments, monitor results, and adjust parameters as conditions change in real time.

mechanisms.reason: The standard shifts routine, previously human-supervised experimental execution to autonomous agent orchestration across multiple devices, though this displaces lab labor rather than seat-based software specifically.
mechanisms.quote: AI into these tools, MHS also helps researchers and engineers more readily orchestrate autonomous, round-the-clock experiments and workflows
